scope: Administration and ACL extension after the completed Phase 0–6 baseline

rubric.accuracy: Authorization, concurrency, retry semantics, catalog integrity, privacy and UI behavior agree with the reviewed design and observed evidence.
rubric.completeness: Requested administration pages, word/hint management, role assignment, private environment bootstrap, documentation and relevant verification are present.
rubric.approvalThreshold: At least 98 in both categories, with no unresolved material finding.
rubric.qualification: Scores express review judgment, not statistical guarantees.

snapshot.algorithm: SHA256 over UTF-8 lines in listed files-array order: file SHA256, two spaces, relative path, LF.
snapshot.independentVerification: All 189 listed file hashes match current files. Recomputed snapshot digest matches the recorded digest.

assessment.authorization: Permissions are derived from authenticated profiles and trusted server configuration. Administrative SQL independently authorizes directory reads and mutations. Browser database roles cannot execute the privileged ACL functions.
assessment.bootstrap: WORDPAIRS_ADMIN_PROFILE_IDS is private server configuration containing explicit profile IDs. There is no first-user assignment, default administrator credential or browser-controlled bootstrap.
assessment.concurrency: Exclusive ACL locking serializes role changes and final-administrator checks. Content operations acquire the corresponding shared lock before loading authoritative roles. The repaired integration test verifies an actual writer waiting behind revocation.
assessment.retries: ACL authorization precedes canonical replay, so revoked administrators cannot recover authority through historical commands. Replayed successful grants do not reapply removed roles. Existing content replay remains mutation-free.
assessment.catalog: Editorial changes append the next immutable pair version without moving IDs between categories. Community activation requires previously unused IDs at version zero. Historical round lookups remain available; future selection uses the highest version and never falls back after exclusion. Both publication paths enforce the 4096-version ceiling.
assessment.interface: Administration pages provide moderation, word/hint editing and user-role management. Identity binding, uncertain-write retries and stale-response invalidation protect private UI state. Reviewed phone captures show readable forms and controls without visible clipping.

resolvedFindings.issue: Publishing beyond 4096 historical versions could make catalog reads unavailable.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Both editorial saves and community activation reject projected overflow before mutation. Pure and PostgreSQL evidence cover rejection and preserved state/history.

resolvedFindings.issue: Newest-selectable wording could imply fallback to an older excluded pair version.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Design explicitly specifies highest-version selection followed by selectability filtering.

resolvedFindings.issue: A delayed authorized GET could repopulate privileged data after mutation denial.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Both private UI owners increment their request generation before clearing data. Browser regressions exercise delayed GET, POST 403 and late GET completion for users and moderation.

resolvedFindings.issue: Community activation bypassed pair identity and version invariants.
resolvedFindings.originalEvidence: Independent execution of the actual domain source accepted heroes-01, originally category heroes/version 0, in hv-weather/version 99.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Activation now requires unused IDs at version zero. Regression assertions separately reject reused IDs at version zero, cross-category reuse and skipped versions.

resolvedFindings.issue: Manifest algorithm description incorrectly claimed ordinal sorting.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Description now specifies listed-files order. Every file hash and the aggregate digest independently reproduce.

finalPostgreSQLSuite.result: 66/66 tests passed across 10 files; migration and SQL checks passed

focusedAdministrationPostgreSQL.scope: Includes actual Request handlers, trusted environment bootstrap and real database persistence; test database TLS factory seam substituted.

evidenceQualifications: The reviewer independently ran the focused 18-test suite, not the full database or browser suites.

Administration browser tests use disclosed HTTP fixtures. The catalog journey exercises the actual content service/domain with an in-memory transaction port; those tests alone do not prove database authorization.
Separate real PostgreSQL and actual route-handler tests supply persistence and server-authorization evidence.
Phone inspection was agent visual review and browser automation; no personal human sign-off or human testing is claimed.

The first full PostgreSQL run passed 65/66 and timed out at 60 seconds in the 25-player fixture. Its failure log is preserved. Increasing only that fixture's wall-clock budget to 120 seconds retained all eight-round assertions; the subsequent complete run passed.
Approval binds to the verified local snapshot, not an independently verified new remote commit.
disposition: The reviewed administration/ACL extension is technically ready and approved. No unresolved material correctness, security, completeness or usability finding remains.
scopeLimits: This extension does not reopen historical Phase 0–6 approvals.
